Issue no. 3: Whether the suit has been filed without cause of action?

OPD.
39.
It is settled law that cause of action consists of a bundle of facts, which gives a ground to enforce a legal right which plaintiff must prove so as to get a judgment in his favor.
In order to decide whether a suit has a subsisting cause of action or not, the court has to look at the plaint and nothing else.
Further, there is a difference between a plea that the plaint does not disclose cause of action and plea that there is no cause of action for instituting a suit.

For determining whether the plaint discloses the cause of action or not, averments in the plaint alone are relevant and the court while deciding this issue need not look into the proof of cause of action.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The plaintiff has to prove personal injuries caused by the business activities run by the defendants since he has filed the present suit in his personal capacity as an individual.
Plaintiff has relied upon Ex.PW1/8 to support his claim that defendants are cooking food at the location in question for their various branches, however, perusal of Ex.PW1/8 merely shows food being delivered or taken in/out and does not substantiate the claim that food is being delivered for other branches.
Furthermore, Ex.PW1/8 is a picture of broad day light and thus,
cannot in any matter support the claim of food being delivered at night.
Accordingly,
plaintiff has failed to substantiate the claim of nuisance.
Additionally, plaintiff has not produced anything on record to prove personal injuries caused to him by the business activities run by the defendants and in such a case, defendants cannot be directed to shut down their business.

32. It is settled position of law and elementary rule of civil litigation that the case of plaintiff must stand on the strength of his/her own and that in respect of relief claimed by a plaintiff, he/she has to stand on his/her own legs by proving his/her case.
While Ex. PW1/10 to PW1/14 shows water damage, there is nothing on record to substantiate that the same is caused by the defendants or the defendants are discharging untreated waste and water affluent in the sewage line.
Plaintiff has neither produced any evidence nor examined any witness to discharge this burden as well and thus, cannot be held entitled to the relief of mandatory injunction.
38. Accordingly, issue no. 2 is decided in favour of the defendants and against the plaintiff.
It is settled law that cause of action consists of a bundle of facts, which gives a ground to enforce a legal right which plaintiff must prove so as to get a judgment in his favor.
In order to decide whether a suit has a subsisting cause of action or not, the court has to look at the plaint and nothing else.
Further, there is a difference between a plea that the plaint does not disclose cause of action and plea that there is no cause of action for instituting a suit.
For determining whether the plaint discloses the cause of action or not, averments in the plaint alone are relevant and the court while deciding this issue need not look into the proof of cause of action.
